newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Petkim targets $864 mln turnover in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Turk Petkim targets $864 mln turnover in 1997.

text.p: Turkey's sole petrochemical products producer Petkim Petrokimya Holding A.S. targets a $864.7 million turnover in 1997, against more than $800 million expected in 1996, a senior company official said.
"We will raise capacity utilisation to 101 percent to meet our 127.3 trillion lira or $864.7 million total sales target in 1997," Mehmet Yilmaz, general manager of Petkim, told Reuters.

He said the 1997 target included $762.1 million of domestic sales and $102.61 million of exports and added that 1996 exports were expected to overshoot to $109 million, from an initial target of $103 million.
Yilmaz said Petkim's 1997 profits were targeted at 23.6 trillion lira, or $160.26 million.
Shares of Petkim closed at 47,000 lira on the Istanbul Stock Exchange on Tuesday, versus 46,500 on Monday.

The company based its target figures on an average dollar rate of 147,265 lira for this year, up from the Turkish government's average lira/dollar rate target of 135,000 lira, according to the 1997 budget.
Petkim estimates inflation to be at 83 percent and the dollar to equal 187,429 lira at the end of 1997, compared to the government targets of 65 percent and 163,000 lira.

The company has two plants, nearby the facilities of state-owned petroleum refiner Tupras in Yarimca/Izmit and Aliaga/Izmir regions on the western coasts Turkey because it buys all of its raw material supplies from Tupras.
Yilmaz said 100.1 trillion lira of the total 127.3-trillion- lira 1997 turnover would be earned from the Aliaga plant.
Petkim is one of the major state firms listed in the Turkish government's privatisation programme after 4.1 percent of its capital was sold to the public in 1987.

Existing shareholders and some officials in Petkim complain that the company's new capacity expansion investments are restricted by the privatisation agency OIB, the main shareholder, as part of the government's sell-off policy.

Petkim which could meet all of the demand for petrochemical products in the domestic market until early 1980's, can currently meet only about 50 percent of the domestic demand after it was included in the country's privatisation scheme.

The company applied to the OIB to allow a 3.57 trillion lira investment in 1996 prices this year, but received approval for 2.76 trillion lira of investments in current prices. It had spent 1.15 trillion lira on modernisation projects in 1996.
"With the modernisation investments, we can get the possibility of expanding our capacities in certain products," the general manager said.
In 1997, Petkim's VCM output capacity will be expanded by six percent while its PVC capacity will be raised to 150,000 tonnes annually, from 140,000 tonnes.
The chlorine-alkali unit's annual capacity will be expanded to 94,000 tonnes from 80,000 tonnes and will later be raised to more than 100,000 tonnes gradually.
The company also plans to expand its YYPE unit by 60 percent to 96,000 tonnes in 1997, from the current 60,000 tonnes.
The company reported 51.14 trillion lira of turnover in the first nine months of 1996 against 41.11 trillion lira in the same 1995 period.
Its net profit increased to 17.1 trillion lira in the first nine months of 1996, from 16.4 trillion lira in the same period of 1995.
